headline: RMG wage board to meet for first time amid worker protests
summary: The board will recommend minimum wage rates for garment workers as employees demand a monthly salary of Tk 30,000.
details: The minimum wage board for the garment sector is set to hold its first meeting today at 11am in Segunbagicha, Dhaka.
The board, presided over by Chairman Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, will recommend minimum wage rates for garment workers and employees.
The government formed the board on Nov 1 while reconstituting the national minimum wage board amid unrest in the sector.
Workers have been agitating in Dhaka for days, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
Tensions have escalated, with garment workers clashing with police in Mirpur on Tuesday during a road blockade.
The current minimum wage, which was raised from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500 in November 2023, is set to expire next month.
Under the Labour Act, the board's recommendations will be based on requests from employers, workers, or both.
caption:
Garment workers are demanding Tk 30,000 per month as the RMG wage board holds its first meeting.

The minimum wage board for the garment sector is set to hold its first meeting today at 11am in Segunbagicha, Dhaka.

The board, presided over by Chairman Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, will recommend minimum wage rates for garment workers and employees.

The government formed the board on Nov 1 while reconstituting the national minimum wage board amid unrest in the sector.

Workers have been agitating in Dhaka for days, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

Tensions have escalated, with garment workers clashing with police in Mirpur on Tuesday during a road blockade.

The current minimum wage, which was raised from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500 in November 2023, is set to expire next month.

Under the Labour Act, the board's recommendations will be based on requests from employers, workers, or both.

headline_marked: Police use [[sound grenades to disperse RMG workers]] in Gazipur
headline: Police use sound grenades to disperse RMG workers in Gazipur
summary: Clashes erupted as workers demanded higher wages, leading to factory closures and the deployment of 25 platoons of security forces.
details: Police fired at least 10 sound grenades to disperse garment workers in Gazipur this morning, following reports that protesters threw bricks and stones at the Basan Police Station.
The unrest occurred despite a decision to reopen all factories from today. Protesters gathered in front of the police station demanding higher wages, briefly blocking roads and disrupting traffic.
The situation caused widespread panic in the areas surrounding the Chandana Chowrasta-Shibbari road. Some factories, including Lyric Group and Odessa Garments, declared holidays for the day.
To bring the situation under control, the district administration has deployed 12 platoons of BGB, five platoons of Ansar, and eight platoons of SRB, totaling 25 platoons of security personnel.
Alongside the security forces, 25 executive magistrates from the district administration are on duty to maintain order in the district.
caption:
Sound grenades fired in Gazipur as RMG workers clash with police over wage demands.

Police fired at least 10 sound grenades to disperse garment workers in Gazipur this morning, following reports that protesters threw bricks and stones at the Basan Police Station.

The unrest occurred despite a decision to reopen all factories from today. Protesters gathered in front of the police station demanding higher wages, briefly blocking roads and disrupting traffic.

The situation caused widespread panic in the areas surrounding the Chandana Chowrasta-Shibbari road. Some factories, including Lyric Group and Odessa Garments, declared holidays for the day.

To bring the situation under control, the district administration has deployed 12 platoons of BGB, five platoons of Ansar, and eight platoons of SRB, totaling 25 platoons of security personnel.

Alongside the security forces, 25 executive magistrates from the district administration are on duty to maintain order in the district.
